## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Dhātubhājanīyakathā* ("The Distribution of the Relics") is the twenty-ninth and concluding chapter of the *Buddhavaṁsa* (Bv 29) [SuttaCentral]. The text recounts the dispersal of the Buddha Gotama's bodily relics following his *parinibbāna* at Kusinārā [Skilling, Ideology of relics]. It opens by declaring that after the Buddha was extinguished at Kusinārā, his relics were distributed across diverse locations (verse 1) [Skilling, Ideology of relics]. Verses 2–12 list the specific relics and their enshrining locations, concluding in verse 13 with the observation that the ancient masters (*porāṇakā*) recorded this distribution of the Great Sage Gotama's relics out of compassion for living beings [Skilling, Ideology of relics].

SuttaCentral notes a thematic connection between this account and the relic distribution related in the *Mahāparinibbāna Sutta* (DN 16) [SuttaCentral]. DharmaNexus records significant Pali-internal text reuse with the Sri Lankan chronicle *Thūpavaṁsa* (8 matching passages, including segments 2.1–3.4) [DharmaNexus], a connection reflected in later secondary literature citing the verses of the *Dhātubhājanīyakathā* in the context of the *Thūpavaṁsa* [Skilling, Ideology of relics]. Additionally, DharmaNexus identifies machine-generated cross-language alignments with Sanskrit Buddhist texts, including the *Āryamañjuśrīmūlakalpa* and the *Caityavandanāstotra* [DharmaNexus].
